result.rationale: The migration inserts each old setting value verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without applying the model's before_validation normalization (`self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` / `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`), while `record_for_host` uses an exact `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` match. Old values with schemes/paths (which the prior spec showed were valid, e.g. 'http://discourse.org') would never match, silently breaking embedding for those hosts after migration.

judged_text: The backfill INSERT copies old setting values verbatim, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//)` and `sub!(/\/.*$/)`) that the new lookup depends on, so old-format entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' — shapes the removed `allows_embeddable_host?` code and its specs explicitly supported — are stored as-is. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`'s exact `lower(host) = uri.host` match never finds those rows, so embedding silently breaks for every host whose old configuration included a scheme or path, even though the migration reported the data as migrated.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` backfills with raw SQL (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`) using the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values verbatim, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips scheme and paths. The new lookup (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` -> `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`) matches only the bare hostname (e.g. `discourse.org`), so rows inserted as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` will never match `uri.host`, breaking host checks post-migration for those legacy formats.
